items.statement: Against laboratory-defined chronic kidney disease stage 3 to 5, a kidney disease code in the network's records has a sensitivity below 70 percent and a positive predictive value of at least 85 percent.
items.rationale: Need is high because a recoding decision depends on it; novelty is modest because the question has been asked elsewhere but not checked here; the data exist and one comparison answers it.
items.risks: Partial verification, practices coding differently, and the definition of the observation window.

items.statement: Sensitivity is lowest in patients aged 80 or over and in stage 3a.
items.rationale: Leads point to older patients; the stage split tells the recoding exercise where to look.

items.statement: About one in ten coded patients has only one low eGFR result, taken during an acute illness.
items.rationale: Quantifies the false-label problem the pharmacist saw.
items.risks: Acute illness is not always coded.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected, with h2 and h3 as pre-specified secondary questions.
